data.raw_text:
Meh…

Some of these alarms are real, but they vary by manufacturer. On a Boeing, the engine fire is just a bell & there is no computer voice telling you which engine it is.

Boeing also doesn’t have a voice warning for the overspeed; it’s just the “clacker” and it’s definitely not scary, more of a “damnit, now we have to do paperwork” thing.

The TCAS “Traffic” alert is sped up in this video. It’s also a pretty common thing to hear & not scary. If it moves from just a traffic advisory to giving you commands to climb or descend, it’s a little more concerning, but I wouldn’t call it scary.

The “Terrain” and “Sink Rate” warnings are higher concerns. Something is going wrong, you probably didn’t notice it was going wrong so you probably don’t know the cause, and it needs to be fixed very quickly.

The “Stall” warning on the 737 is just the “stick shaker”, which rattles the yoke quickly & that can be heard even above the engines & wind rush. If kids come to the cockpit before the flight, we like to joke they are the “machine guns” & press a button which tests the shakers.
